title: Officely vs. OfficeSpace: Which Hybrid Work Platform Fits Your Team?
summary: Compare Officely and OfficeSpace for hybrid work scheduling, desk booking, Slack and Microsoft Teams integration, policy controls, and workplace analytics.
body_markdown:
If you're comparing hybrid work tools, you've probably come across both Officely and OfficeSpace. They sound similar on the surface, but they're built for different jobs.


OfficeSpace is a full workplace and real-estate management suite, with space planning, asset tracking, and facilities operations as its core. Officely is a focused hybrid work and desk booking tool that lives inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, built to get your team coordinating office days fast, without a long rollout.


Here's how they actually compare.


## The quick answer


**Choose OfficeSpace if** you manage a large, multi-site real estate portfolio and need space planning, move management, and asset tracking alongside desk booking.


**Choose Officely if** you want your team to plan office days, book desks, and see who's coming in, all from Slack or Teams, without managing a separate facilities platform.


## Where the platforms differ


### Hybrid work scheduling


Officely is built around a simple idea: office days should be planned, not guessed at. Employees pick their in-office days, teams can coordinate around each other, and managers get visibility into who's actually coming in and when. It's designed to make attendance intentional instead of random, and it happens right where your team already works.


OfficeSpace handles scheduling too, but it sits inside a much bigger system. Space planning, scenario modeling, and portfolio-level reporting are where it's strongest, and attendance scheduling is one piece of a larger operational suite built for facilities and real estate teams.


### Desk booking and hot-desking


Both platforms support desk booking and hot-desking. Officely keeps this simple: reserve a desk in advance, support flexible seating, and reduce the need for fixed desk allocation. **Neighbourhoods** let teams sit near each other on their in-office days, which keeps collaboration easy without adding complexity.


OfficeSpace's booking system is layered on top of interactive digital floor plans, with features like occupancy heat maps, sensor-based auto check-in and release, and proximity-aware booking. If your team needs that level of space-planning detail, OfficeSpace has it. If you want booking to be fast and friction-free for employees, Officely's approach is lighter by design.


### Slack and Microsoft Teams integration


This is where the two platforms pull apart the most. Officely's strongest differentiator is that it works **inside** Slack and Microsoft Teams. Employees book desks, set office days, and check who's in, all without leaving the tools they already use every day. That's a big part of why teams adopt it quickly: there's no new app to learn.


OfficeSpace also connects to Slack and Teams, letting users book through slash commands and receive notifications there. But Slack and Teams access sits alongside a dedicated OfficeSpace web platform and mobile app, which is where most of its planning and reporting work happens. For teams that want everything to happen in chat, Officely is built around that experience from the ground up.


### Approvals and policy controls


Officely gives admins and managers control over attendance workflows where it matters: approvals, exceptions, and oversight of office capacity or team schedules. It also helps you manage **hybrid work policy compliance** , including minimum office day requirements. Managers can see whether attendance expectations are being met, which makes policies easier to enforce fairly and consistently across teams.


OfficeSpace offers policy and request management too, built into its broader facility request and work order system, which also handles maintenance tickets and asset-related requests through integrations like ServiceNow and Jira.


### Workplace analytics


Officely's analytics are built for the People, Workplace, and Operations teams who need to understand office attendance and utilisation, so they can make better decisions about space and policy without wading through a facilities dashboard built for someone else's job.


OfficeSpace's reporting goes deeper into real estate operations: cost-per-seat, cost-per-square-foot, portfolio rollups across multiple sites, and industry benchmarking. That depth is valuable if you're managing real estate at scale, but it's more than most hybrid teams need day to day.


## Where OfficeSpace makes sense


OfficeSpace is a strong fit if your organization manages **multiple large sites** , needs space planning and move management (block-and-stack, scenario modeling), or tracks physical assets alongside desk and room booking. It's built for facilities and corporate real estate teams running complex, multi-site portfolios, and it brings that operational depth as its core strength.


## Where Officely makes sense


Officely is built for hybrid teams, HR and People teams, and Workplace or IT teams who want office coordination to work simply, inside Slack and Microsoft Teams, without taking on a facilities management platform. If your priority is getting people to plan office days, book desks, follow attendance policy, and see utilisation data, without a long implementation or a tool nobody opens, Officely is the more practical fit.


## Try it in your workspace


The best way to see the difference is to try booking a desk or setting an office day directly in Slack or Teams.

No separate app. No long rollout. Just hybrid work, coordinated where your team already talks.
